input.snapshot_context: Frozen export contains Imperium 1.0.1 and Satiscraftory 1.0.0; it predates the separate pack update to Satiscraftory 1.1.0. All comparisons use this same frozen export, replacing AuramCore with the tested 1.0.6 jar.

limitations: The isolated VM has four actual virtual CPUs but uses ARM64 hardware; Akliz uses x86-64.
Fresh world load is controlled; it does not recreate the existing player factory and loaded-world state.
incidental_tool_writes: The initial ServerPackCreator --help invocation re-saved /Users/cyberpwn/serverpackcreator.properties and wrote its usual logs. Subsequent export uses --home /tmp/auram-serverpack-tool/home.
fixture_notes: No connected players; entity-section tracking differed between the minimal and full packs. The final workload serializes 128 untracked capability-heavy ArmorStand objects and compares their held-item NBT once per tick, independently of visibility.
FULL chunk requests are synchronous on the Minecraft server thread, reproducing chunk-load stalls rather than maximum asynchronous pregenerator throughput.
Five warmup batches of four FULL chunks, then twenty measured batches of four FULL chunks per JVM. Two JVM runs per configuration, rotated order.

worker_configuration.reason: ThreadTweak replaces Util background executor using threadCount.main; vanilla max.bg.threads does not control that replacement.
